files.asset_inspection: MS Windows icon resource containing 3 embedded raster frames (16x16, 32x32, 48x48), each PNG-compressed, 8-bit/color RGBA, 32 bits per pixel (verified with `file` and Pillow: sizes {(16,16),(32,32),(48,48)}). Visually it is Droppy's rounded-square app mark: an ultramarine/cobalt-blue tile with a faint binary-digit (0/1) texture behind a pale-blue water-drop silhouette that has two small white oval 'eyes', giving the drop a simple face. Rendering the 48x48 frame to PNG for inspection (im.convert('RGBA')) confirms the same drop-with-eyes glyph as the app icon shown in og-home.png and in the Credits/About Droppy logo, just flattened for favicon use with no rounded-corner alpha mask cut at these small sizes (the icon fills the square). File size grew from 6,862 to 7,504 bytes between B2 and B3 (`git diff --stat` on the pinned commits: 'Bin 6862 -> 7504 bytes'), consistent with a re-exported icon at a new fill color rather than a resize.
files.purpose: This is the marketing website's own <link rel="icon"> favicon, served from /assets/brand/favicon.ico and referenced with `sizes="any"` by website/index.html:46 and website/changelog.html:43; it controls the tab/bookmark icon shown by browsers visiting getdroppycode.app, and has no reader beyond web browsers and crawlers. It is unrelated to any in-app 'favicon' feature (those are the chat-link favicon fetcher in DroppyCode/UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift and the Hydra-merge popover's host favicon in DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/HydraMergePopover.swift, both of which fetch a *remote site's* /favicon.ico at runtime and never touch this file).
feature_notes: The bundle's B2->B3 churn is listed as 0, but that is only true in the line-count sense that applies to any binary blob (line_count is null in porting/source_inventory.json for both files, so a numstat necessarily reads 0/0). The file's *content* did change between B2 and HEAD: `git log 1fbf81e61e28a079508a074c01ee1830a9cc23dc..HEAD -- website/assets/brand/favicon.ico` shows exactly one intervening commit, 280e05d8b 'Icon: Droppy's new ultramarine art-style blue', and `git diff --stat` over the same range reports 'Bin 6862 -> 7504 bytes'. The computed sha256 (463335e2c215e224d2df34349b50f072b4841348468435be0cc8db2fad0afd7e) matches both the inventory's recorded sha256 and the B3 git blob df86aa718eb1659893737551ca2c9ffd5dc4e153, confirming the file at E:\Droppy\reference\droppy-code-v1.7.0 is the post-rebrand B3 asset, not the pre-rebrand B2 one.

porting/source_inventory.json flags both files with inclusion_evidence 'may supply runtime content (changelog/update feed) - must be checked'. Checked: porting/spec/UPDATE.json (PR-UPDATE-005/018/019 and neighbors) documents the update feed as one unauthenticated GET to the GitLab releases API (https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/86415974/releases), and on Windows (OD-0008 C6, OD-0012 I1) that feed value is an internal, empty-by-default setting with no network call at all until the owner supplies one; nothing in that flow fetches getdroppycode.app, favicon.ico or og-home.png. The only other appearances of the getdroppycode.app domain in the spec (porting/spec/UPDATE.json and SETTINGS.json) are plain-text attribution strings in the About/Credits card ('Based on Droppy Code by Jordy Spruit (Droppy), https://getdroppycode.app'), not fetches of this asset. So the flag resolves to 'no': this file supplies no app runtime content.

files.asset_inspection: 1200x630 PNG, 8-bit/color RGBA, non-interlaced (per `file`) - the standard Open Graph/Twitter-card social preview size. Visually: a near-black background tiled with a faint repeating pattern of small binary digits (0s and 1s); centered near the top is the same ultramarine rounded-square app icon as the favicon (binary-digit texture behind a pale-blue water-drop face with two white eyes). Below it, bold white/blue headline text reads 'All your coding agents, one native  Mac app' (with 'coding agents' set in a lighter blue and an Apple glyph before 'Mac app'), then a gray subheading 'Streaming replies, inline approvals, a diff for every turn. Free and open source.' At the bottom, a small droplet-with-padlock badge icon sits beside the line 'The coding app by Droppy'. File size grew from 135,966 to 147,893 bytes between B2 and B3 (git diff --stat, same commit range as the favicon), consistent with the same icon-recolor re-export rather than a text or layout change (the visible copy text is unchanged from B2's marketing claims).
files.purpose: This is the Open Graph / Twitter-card share image for the marketing homepage, referenced (with a `?v=3` cache-busting query) by og:image, og:image:secure_url and twitter:image meta tags in website/index.html:31-42 and website/changelog.html:28-39; it is what link previews (Slack, X/Twitter, iMessage, Discord, etc.) render when someone shares getdroppycode.app or its changelog page. Like the favicon it is fetched only by social-media crawlers and browsers rendering the public website, never by the Windows app.
ui_elements: website/changelog.html:28-39 identical og:image / og:image:secure_url / twitter:image tags pointing at the same file
feature_notes: Same B2->B3 churn-label caveat as the favicon: line_count is null (binary), so the bundle's numeric 'churn 0' reflects the absence of text-line diffing, not an unchanged file. `git log 1fbf81e61e28a079508a074c01ee1830a9cc23dc..HEAD -- website/assets/og/og-home.png` shows the same single commit, 280e05d8b 'Icon: Droppy's new ultramarine art-style blue', and `git diff --stat` reports 'Bin 135966 -> 147893 bytes'. Computed sha256 (4b935b054b5fff99534df9ada74ee2317cd135059dcaafbfbddff2394534533b) matches the inventory's recorded sha256 and the B3 git blob d292bd81db0732ad31146efac3a6a648c9fd58c9 exactly, so the reference tree holds the rebranded (ultramarine) B3 image, not the B2 predecessor.

The og:image URLs carry a manual '?v=3' cache-busting suffix in both website/index.html and website/changelog.html; that suffix is part of the HTML text (not this asset) and was not itself part of this bundle, but its presence corroborates that the maintainers version-stamped a deliberate image update rather than an incidental re-save.

Same runtime-content check as the favicon (porting/source_inventory.json's 'may supply runtime content (changelog/update feed) - must be checked' flag): the app's update/changelog mechanism talks only to the GitLab releases API, never to getdroppycode.app's asset paths, so this image supplies no runtime content to the Windows app either.
